prerequisites: knowledge of basic concepts from mechanics: force, velocity, acceleration
Proof of participation in a calibration test is required for courses in the Bachelor of Engineering Science and Bachelor of Engineering Science: Architecture programs.

learning_outcomes.text: The student knows the basic concepts of statics, kinematics and dynamics of rigid bodies in three-dimensional space.

The student understands the connections between the basic quantities in statics, kinematics, and dynamics of rigid bodies in three-dimensional space, and can mathematically translate these connections into scalar and vector equations.
The student can apply the basic laws of statics for rigid bodies in three-dimensional space.
The student can apply the basic laws of kinematics for rigid bodies in three-dimensional space.
The student can apply the basic laws of dynamics for rigid bodies in planar motion or motions that can be reduced to it.
The student relates the physical concepts (force, moment, displacement, velocity, acceleration) to the mathematical form and properties of the equations.
The student can perform an analysis of equilibrium and/or motion for a simple concrete technical realization.
The student becomes familiar with the orders of magnitude of mechanical quantities.
"Rigid bodies" refers to both single rigid bodies and composite bodies consisting of a chain of single rigid bodies (e.g., mechanisms).
Students develop the following attitudes: meticulousness, a critical attitude, and independence.

syllabus_topics: Statics, kinematics and dynamics of single bodies (First Semester)
Basic elements of statics: classification of forces, vectorial equilibrium conditions of single bodies including friction.
Kinematics: motion of a point, and the (compound) motion of single bodies.

Fundamental concepts of dynamics: Newton's postulates, derivation of the basic laws of dynamics of material systems (impulse law and energy law), associated conservation law formulations, introduction to the dynamics of single objects via two-dimensional motion.
Statics, kinematics and dynamics of composite bodies (Second Semester)
Method of virtual work for solving statics problems.
Vectorial equilibrium conditions of composite bodies including friction.
Dynamics of composite bodies in two-dimensional motion.
Method of virtual work for solving statics problems of both single and composite bodies.
teaching_methods: Exercise sessions (small group independent work, self-study with support)
assessment_rules: A midterm test is organized in the first semester, followed by a partial exam in January and a partial exam in June. The score after the first examination period is the January exam score. If the student passed the midterm test and achieved a better result on it than on the January exam, the midterm test result is factored into the first exam period score with a ratio of 75% for the January exam and 25% for the midterm test. For the second examination period, if the student scores at least 8/20 on the June exam and achieved a higher score in the first semester than on the June exam, the first examination period result is factored into the second exam period score with a ratio of 60% for the June exam and 40% for the first exam period score (including any midterm test calculation). During the third examination period, the entire course is evaluated through a single resit exam, and no midterm test or first exam period scores are carried over. Rounding is usually standard, but if at least half of the questions are deficient, rounding is always downwards.
